content: The interaction between isoflurane and posaconazole can lead to an increased QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Similarly, posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ivosidenib should be avoided or replaced with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, the ivosidenib dose should be reduced to 250 mg daily, and if the inhibitor is discontinued, the dose can be increased back to 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Both ivosidenib and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval, so their co-administration should be avoided or replaced with alternative therapies. If co-administration is unavoidable, patients should be monitored for an increased risk of QTc prolongation. Posaconazole also increases the levels or effects of ketamine, larotrectinib, lasmiditan, lefamulin, lemborexant, leniolisib, and lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations should be avoided or replaced with alternative drugs. If larotrectinib is co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, its dose should be reduced by 50%, and the original dose can be resumed after the inhibitor is discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. Lasmiditan increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition, and this combination should be avoided or replaced. Posaconazole also increases the levels or effects of macitentan, mefloquine, midazolam (intranasal), midostaurin, mirtazapine, neratinib, nirogacestat, olaparib, omaveloxolone, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, and dasabuvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations should be avoided or replaced with alternative drugs. If unavoidable, dose adjustments and close monitoring are required. Posaconazole and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval, and their co-administration should be avoided, especially in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when used with other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. Posaconazole also increases the levels or effects of osimertinib, oxaliplatin, oxycodone, palbociclib, palovarotene, panobinostat, pazopanib, pemigatinib, pexidartinib, phenytoin, pimavanserin, pimozide, pirtobrutinib, pitolisant, pomalidomide, ponatinib, pralsetinib, procainamide, quinidine, ranolazine, red yeast rice, repotrectinib, ribociclib, rifabutin, rimegepant, riociguat, rivaroxaban, ruxolitinib, Saccharomyces boulardii, selpercatinib, selumetinib, sevoflurane, silodosin, siponimod, sirolimus, solifenacin, sonidegib, sorafenib, sotalol, sparsentan, stiripentol, suvorexant, tacrolimus, tamsulosin, tazemetostat, teniposide, tepotinib, tetrabenazine, tiagabine, tofacitinib, tolvaptan, trabectedin, tramadol, trazodone, ubrogepant, umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol, vandetanib, vemurafenib, vilazodone, vinblastine, vincristine, vincristine liposomal, vorapaxar, and voriconazole. These interactions occur primarily through CYP3A4 inhibition or QTc prolongation, and co-administration should generally be avoided or replaced with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, dose adjustments, close monitoring, and ECG evaluations are necessary. Posaconazole also interacts with albuterol, alfuzosin, almotriptan, alprazolam, aluminum hydroxide, amiodarone, amitriptyline, amlodipine, amoxapine, apalutamide, aprepitant, arformoterol, aripiprazole, artemether/lumefantrine, atogepant, atomoxetine, atorvastatin, bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens, bedaquiline, benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen, and other drugs. These interactions may involve QTc prolongation, CYP3A4 inhibition, or other mechanisms, requiring caution, dose adjustments, or alternative therapies.
